expectations.text: Applies the two-step test: Annex I (high criticality) vs Annex II sectors, then size thresholds (generally 250+/€50M for essential in Annex I; medium-size entities typically important)
expectations.evidence: Misstates the size step: 'Within Annex I sectors, medium and large entities (50+ employees or €10M+...) are essential entities' — contradicts ground truth that medium-size Annex I entities are typically important (250+/€50M for essential)

expectations.text: States the supervision difference: essential = ex-ante AND ex-post (inspections, audits); important = ex-post only, triggered by evidence
expectations.evidence: Essential entities are subject to proactive, ex-ante supervision... Important entities are subject to reactive, ex-post supervision only — the authority generally only investigates after evidence

expectations.text: States the fine floors: ≥€10M or 2% worldwide turnover (essential) vs ≥€7M or 1.4% (important)
expectations.evidence: fines up to €10,000,000 or 2% of total global annual turnover... important entities face up to €7,000,000 or 1.4%

expectations.text: Mentions management liability including potential temporary bans from managerial functions (essential entities)
expectations.evidence: No mention of management/board personal liability or temporary bans from managerial functions anywhere in the response

expectations.text: Notes special designations: CER-designated critical entities are automatically essential regardless of size; some sectors (e.g., qualified trust/DNS/TLD) essential regardless of size
expectations.evidence: Regardless of size, an entity is automatically essential if it is... identified as critical under the separate CER Directive... qualified trust service provider or TLD registry/DNS provider (these are essential regardless of size)
